content: {"rules": ["Model forecasts tend to overestimate prices in early cycles and show mean-reversion bias later.", "Sentiment spikes correlate with forecast overshoots, especially when sentiment rises above 0.67.", "Forecast accuracy improves when sentiment history shows sustained positive momentum.", "Model lag is evident when true prices dip below forecast mid-cycle, indicating delayed reaction to sentiment shifts.", "High sentiment volatility (e.g., -0.33) correlates with forecast underperformance in subsequent periods.", "Forecast bias is strongest in the first 10 days of the 30-day window, with later days showing stronger mean-reversion.", "Sentiment history with multiple 1.00 values predicts higher forecast accuracy and less overshoot.", "Model forecasts should be adjusted downward when sentiment shows negative spikes or sudden drops."]}
